signature_moves: Rounded geometric bold sans (Poppins/Nunito-class) as the sole warmth vector on an otherwise greyscale charcoal utility
Destination-as-card dashboard: each predefined email target is a droppable tile with a large green 'send' affordance (recognition over recall; big drag-drop Fitts targets)
Single-hue accent economy — one pistachio green (#BEE294) does wordmark, primary action, and brand pills; no second accent
Two-tone 'dropa'(green)/'doo'(grey) wordmark echoing the green-paperclip-on-charcoal app icon
defects: Contrast Dilution — secondary email text ~3.6:1 and dim gear ~2.1:1 on the card fill fall below WCAG floors; de-emphasis crosses the contrast floor

Non-native chrome (native tells, excluded from macOS canon) — in-window hamburger menu instead of the menu bar; grey faux/inactive traffic lights on the hero window; app brand-green used as the control accent instead of the system accent; non-SF-Pro brand typeface; no native materials

aesthetic.direction: friendly-dark utility — Playful/toy rounded-sans warmth grafted onto a restrained dark-neutral (Neo-grotesque-product) surface, single-accent
peers: indie menu-bar file utilities (Dropzone / CleanShot register)
but with a rounded-brand-font twist unlike those SF-Pro-native tools

psychology: Jakob's Law — VIOLATED: hamburger menu, faux traffic lights, and non-native chrome defy the macOS conventions users arrive expecting (menu bar, coloured window controls), adding avoidable friction
Fitts's Law — EXPLOITED: large card drop-targets make the core drag-and-drop action low-error by design
Recognition over recall — EXPLOITED: each destination card shows name + address + subject template, so users pick a target by sight, not memory
Hick's Law — EXPLOITED: 'does exactly one thing'; a small fixed set of predefined destinations keeps the decision trivial
Von Restorff / accent economy — PARTIAL: the single green pops the send action against charcoal, but green also on wordmark + hamburger line slightly dilutes the 'one different thing'
Aesthetic-Usability effect — the committed rounded-friendly look buys perceived usability; the sub-floor secondary-text contrast is the crack the halo is papering over
notes: ONLY a marketing composite (cover.png) was available — no real screenshot, no shots[]. The app window is scaled by an unknown factor, so colours are reliable (measured from flat regions) but ALL sizes are relative/estimated and absolute pt is unrecoverable; re-digest if a true @2x screenshot arrives. The composite also contains a Finder window that is a PLATFORM PROP (genuine macOS 26 Liquid Glass Finder — white body, circular glass toolbar buttons, SF Pro, German locale 'Suchen/Objekte/verfügbar' illustrating the drag source); its tokens are Finder's, NOT dropadoo's, and were excluded. Notable contradiction worth flagging to synthesis: the prop Finder is authentically native while dropadoo's own window is deliberately non-native — the developer clearly knows the native look and chose to depart from it. The app icon (icon.png, not digested here — Workflow A is UI-only) is a charcoal squircle with a light envelope flap + green paperclip, reinforcing the same #BEE294-on-charcoal identity. Lineage set to web-electron at LOW confidence purely as the best-fit non-native bucket (card-grid + hamburger + custom chrome); it may be Flutter/Tauri/custom-SwiftUI — the load-bearing fact is only that it is not AppKit-native and must not feed macOS canon.
